Set the polygonal resolution for this model.

Hot keys: D - decrease resolution, Ctrl+D increase resolution

High resolution (full segments in the branches, highest LOD meshes, all nodes computed).

Hot keys: D - decrease resolution, Ctrl+D increase resolution

Medium resolution (reduced segments in the branches, second LOD meshes, some nodes removed).

Hot keys: D - decrease resolution, Ctrl+D increase resolution

Low resolution (significantly reduced segments in the branches, lowest LOD meshes, many nodes removed).

Hot keys: D - decrease resolution, Ctrl+D increase resolution

Draft resolution (ultra low resolution everywhere, intended for fast computing and workflow acceleration only).

Hot keys: D - decrease resolution, Ctrl+D increase resolution
Control which geometry types are shown in the viewport.
Specify the style in which the scene is rendered.

Zoom the camera view to show the selection.  If nothing is selected, zoom out far enough to show the whole model.

Hot key: Z

Click this button and then click any spot on the model to set the view's
pivot point on that part of the model.  The camera will zoom to and pivot around
the selected point.

Hot key: N
('double-clicking' anywhere on the model is a shortcut for this action)

Toggle between editing generators and nodes.  Nodes are individual parts of the tree (like a leaf
or a branch).  Generators are groups of nodes that represent a section of the model. Most editing
should be done on the generators to efficiently control large portions of the model.  Switch to editing
nodes to fine tune the model before exporting.

Hot key: Tab

All property edits apply to the selected node(s).  Property edits in this mode are offsets to the
the value computed by the generator and should be used for fine tuning only.

Hot key: Tab

All property edits apply to the selected generator(s).  This mode affects all of the individuals nodes
created by the generator(s) and allows parent curve editing.

Hot key: Tab

Add geometry to the model based on a set of predefined templates.  Once a template has been added,
select any of the new generators to edit the model.

Control how much of the model is visible.  Use these options to
temporarily reduce computing and rendering complexity.

Set the season of the current model.  This is applicable to any models that makes use of the season
properties on generators and the season curves on materials.

Hot key: Alt+S
Set options for the transform gizmo.

Compute ambient occlusion on the model. Once computed, ambient occlusion settings can be edited
by selecting the light.  Recomputing the tree will clear AO values.


Hot key: O

Eliminate colliding leaf meshes.  Meshes are removed in the background according to the quality setting:

High:		leaf-leaf and leaf-branch collisions are eliminated, as many leaves as possible remain (slowest)
Medium:	leaf-leaf and leaf-branch collisions are eliminated, more leaves are removed in favor of faster execution
Low:		most leaf-leaf collision are eliminated, leaf-branch collisions are ignored
None:		collisions are ignored
Export the model as a mesh (including animation, unwrapped textures, hierarchy, and other features if desired).

Access force functions.  Forces are modeling tools that manipulate growth in world-space.  Examples
of their use include gravity (downward direction forces) and growing geometry around 3d
geometry (mesh forces)

Hot key: 6 (toggles forces in the viewport)

Access collision object functions.  Collision objects are simple geometric primitives
that can be accessed via the SDK to assist with collision at run-time.

Hot key: 7 (toggles collision objects in the viewport)

Access high level wind functions.  Wind is controlled by a combination of properties in the
model (typically in the 'Wind' group) and properties of the fan object.

Hot key: 8 (toggles wind)
Enable this option to speed up computation time during edits.
Select which tool is used for selected scene objects.
